subject: Mutual action plan & evaluation timeline — TTFT + streaming latency tests
messages:
From: Jordan Leigh <jordan.leigh@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Nobles <samira.nobles@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Eval scope + timing request — TTFT/streaming latency for chat

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo today — Acme's product team wants to formalize the evaluation so we can lock the procurement timeline. We have a short MAP to align on (TIMELINE: 3 weeks) and a focused performance scope: time-to-first-token (TTFT) and streaming tail latencies for chat/text generation across expected concurrencies.

Key asks from our side:
- TTFT (streaming) p50/p95/p99 for prompt sizes ~64 / 256 / 512 tokens
- Tail latencies at concurrencies: 1, 8, 32 (and an auto-scaling note if throughput drops)
- End-to-end throughput (tokens/sec) under sustained load (10m window)
- Test environment details (model variant, quantization, instance type) and any caching/batching enabled
- Raw metrics and a short summary PDF we can include in the MAP

I've attached our initial eval spec (acme-eval-spec.xlsx) with sample prompts and acceptance criteria. Our internal target: p95 TTFT <= 350ms at concurrency 8 for ~256-token responses. If Redwood can show a plan + concrete numbers we can move to PO in the week after the results review.

Can you confirm availability to run the tests next week and a proposed MAP with owners/dates?

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Platform Integrations
Acme Health

Attachment: acme-eval-spec.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Leigh <jordan.leigh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval scope + timing request — TTFT/streaming latency for chat

Jordan — thanks for the clear spec and for the target. We can run the suite and deliver a concise MAP (owners, milestones, acceptance criteria) plus the results pack you described. High-level proposal:

Mutual Action Plan (summary)
- Sep 14: Baseline runs (single-concurrency; verify model variant and quantization) — owner: Dylan (SE)
- Sep 15–16: Streaming TTFT & concurrency sweep (1 / 8 / 32) with 64/256/512-token responses — owner: Dylan
- Sep 17: Internal analysis + generate summary PDF and raw CSVs — owner: Marissa (Solutions)
- Sep 18: Results review + decision call with Acme (30m) — attendees: Jordan, Samira, Vanessa, Dylan, Marissa
- Sep 20: Optional canary plan if results meet acceptance criteria — owner: Vanessa

Acceptance criteria (draft)
- p95 TTFT <= 350ms at concurrency 8 for 256-token outputs
- p99 TTFT improvement plan or fallback model variant if p99 > 700ms
- Sustained throughput of >= 8k tokens/sec for the 10m window at concurrency 32 (acme target)

We will run tests on the Redwood Dedicated test pool (H100-80GB profile) using the rw-instruct-70B quantized profile we discussed (int8). We will run both streaming and non-streaming extraction paths with prefix cache enabled to mirror production traffic.

I'll let Dylan confirm exact run parameters; Marissa will assemble the PDF for your architecture/ procurement folder.

Can we lock Sep 14 for the baseline? If that works we'll post the MAP and calendar invites.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Leigh <jordan.leigh@acmehealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T18:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval scope + timing request — TTFT/streaming latency for chat

Jordan / team — we completed the test runs today on the Dedicated H100-80GB pool, model rw-instruct-70B (int8 quant profile), continuous batching disabled for the TTFT runs (we measured both with and without autoscaler batching — see notes). Attached: redwood-streaming-results-summary.pdf and acme-eval-raw-results.csv. Highlights below.

Test notes (short):
- Load generator: custom harness mimicking client-side streaming (tokens flushed on first chunk)
- Prefix KV cache: enabled for half the runs to reflect warm state; cold runs also included
- Sequence profiles: short (64), mid (256), long (512) tokens; all run at concurrencies 1 / 8 / 32 (sustained 10-minute windows)
- Measured TTFT (streaming = time from request to first token emitted) and completion latency for non-streaming path.

Summary results (streaming TTFT) — values in milliseconds
- Concurrency 1:
  - 64 tokens: p50 78ms, p95 162ms, p99 320ms
  - 256 tokens: p50 120ms, p95 240ms, p99 420ms
  - 512 tokens: p50 170ms, p95 330ms, p99 620ms
- Concurrency 8:
  - 64 tokens: p50 95ms, p95 210ms, p99 380ms
  - 256 tokens: p50 140ms, p95 295ms, p99 560ms
  - 512 tokens: p50 205ms, p95 420ms, p99 780ms
- Concurrency 32:
  - 64 tokens: p50 160ms, p95 420ms, p99 820ms
  - 256 tokens: p50 260ms, p95 610ms, p99 1130ms
  - 512 tokens: p50 410ms, p95 980ms, p99 1750ms

Throughput (tokens/sec sustained, 10m window) — measured across test pool (aggregate)
- Concurrency 8 (256-token profile): 9,600 tokens/sec
- Concurrency 32 (256-token profile): 26,500 tokens/sec (note: this includes tail retries for cold-start buckets)

Observations & recommendations
- Warm prefix cache reduces p95 by ~20–30% for mid/long responses; we recommend a warm-cache canary for initial rollout.
- For strict p99 SLAs at concurrency 32 for 512-token outputs, consider an alternative model variant (rw-instruct-30B int8) as a fallback — p99s for the 30B variant were ~60% lower in our baseline sweep (details in CSV).
- Continuous batching helped throughput but increased TTFT p50 by ~25ms; we report both modes in the CSV so you can weigh latency vs unit-cost tradeoffs.

Attached files: redwood-streaming-results-summary.pdf (2-page PDF), acme-eval-raw-results.csv (full samples + histograms).

Next steps we propose:
- Sep 15: Review call (15–30m) to walk the PDF and acceptance-line items (we can adjust MAP if you want a different p95/p99 target).
- Sep 20: If accepted, we can schedule a two-week canary with warm-cache provisioning and a throttled roll (we will provide monitoring dashboards).

If you want any additional concurrency points (e.g., 16 or 64) or different sequence distributions, let me know and we can re-run — these runs took ~3 hours each for the 10m sustained window.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

Team — this is great, thanks for the thorough sweeps and clear breakdown. A few quick notes from our side: we reviewed the PDF and the CSV and agree with the warm-cache canary approach.

Decisions / Next steps
- Accept MAP as proposed; Sep 15 review call confirmed (we scheduled a 30m review at 16:00 PT)
- Acceptance criteria: p95 TTFT <= 350ms at concurrency 8 for 256-token payloads (as long as warm-cache is used during canary)
- Canary: Sep 20–Oct 04 (2-week window) with error budget monitor; we'll sign PO contingent on canary health and the dashboard thresholds you provide

Please share the meeting invite and the Drive link to the raw results (I used the PDF in our procurement folder).

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Platform Integrations — Acme Health
